title: GitHub - timjonez/new-english-dictionary: Page-file transcription of Murray's New English Dictionary for contributors.
excerpt: Page-file transcription of Murray's New English Dictionary for contributors. - timjonez/new-english-dictionary
content_html:
Got leftover usage on an AI subscription? Spend it here. The way to contribute is to point your AI agent at this repository and let it run. It keeps transcribing scans of Murray's New English Dictionary into a public-domain text anyone can use. The 1888–1928 text is being transcribed into the public domain. The scans are A New English Dictionary on Historical Principles, 10 volumes with supplement on Archive.org. Volume 03-DE in that item is only about half the volume, so D and E come from oed03arch.

Everything in this repository is CC0 1.0. Use the transcription, the page files, and the code for anything.

Progress

A snapshot as of 2026-10-27. There are 117 page files under text/, all in 01-AB: scans 25–141. Of those, 112 are draft, 3 are partial (scans 47–49), and 2 are ok (scans 133 and 134). No other volume has a page file yet. The repository does not record how many scans each volume has, so these are counts, not percentages. To see the current state, list text/ and read the status line at the top of each file.

Contribute

You need:

  • a GitHub account and git
  • uv, to run the checker
  • qpdf, to pull one page out of a volume PDF
  • curl, to download the volume PDF from Archive.org
  • gh, the GitHub CLI, which AGENTS.md uses to read and open pull requests
  • an AI coding agent that can run shell commands and read a PDF page

Point your agent at https://github.com/timjonez/new-english-dictionary and tell it to follow AGENTS.md. That file names each volume PDF and shows how to pull one page out of it with qpdf. Before it transcribes, it claims a scan range with a draft pull request, so two agents do not take the same pages. Let the agent keep going on that branch. It writes one file per scan under text/ and checks each file with uv run pagefile.py. When it stops, that same pull request holds all of those pages.

PROMPT.md is a prompt you can paste into your agent as it is:

Read AGENTS.md and follow it. Keep transcribing pages for the whole session. One pull request holds every page from that run. The format is SPEC.md. Check the files with `uv run pagefile.py`.

Leave the database alone. Do not start other agents.

Read each finished page against the scan again. Paste the `uv run pagefile.py` flag list into the pull request. Keep a flagged spelling when the scan shows it.

The format document is SPEC.md. The checker command is uv run pagefile.py. The agent document is AGENTS.md. The checker exits 0 even when it flags tokens it is unsure of. Compare each flagged token with the scan and include the flag list in your pull request.

Finding a free range

Before you claim scans, look at the open pull requests. A draft pull request titled with a volume and a scan range, such as 01-AB 200-220, is a claim, and those scans are taken. A claim with no push for 48 hours has expired. Also skip any scan that already has a file under text/. Start at the first scan in a volume that has neither, and claim a block you expect to finish. AGENTS.md has the full steps.

Page files already under text/ are done. Scans 25–132 were recovered from the maintainer's database and are draft, except scans 47–49, which stay partial. Leave a finished scan unless you are correcting a reading. Leave the low-resolution 07-OP scan and the 1933 supplement alone.

Worked pages: text/01-AB/0133.md (folio 109) and text/01-AB/0134.md (folio 110).

uv run build.py -o out.sqlite builds a database from the page files. Pass a new path. The command refuses to replace an existing file.
